sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Heerenveen, in Friesland, charges for parking in its centre and in the surrounding streets, and plans to put the car in garages. The council adopted the parking tax ordinance for 2026 on 11 December 2025. At machines in the centre parking costs 1.90 euros an hour, with a day rate of 9.00 euros for stays longer than 4 hours 45 minutes, while on the west side of the railway station it costs 2.50 euros for half a day and 5.00 euros for a whole day [0]. The centre rate is about 6 percent higher than in 2025, and the station rates are unchanged [2]. The standard permit fee is 105 euros a year [1]. Under the 2023 designation, which the register still shows as in force, paid parking applies Monday to Friday from 9:00 to 20:00, Thursday until 21:00 and Saturday until 20:00, and is free on Sundays and holidays; around the centre there are permit-only zones with hours from 9:00 to 17:00 [4][5]. On 29 January 2026 the council adopted a Mobility Fund ordinance for the town centre, under which developers who cannot provide the parking required by the norms can pay between 6,318 and 18,954 euros per space, and the municipality must build the bought-out spaces within ten years or refund the money [6]. The mobility programme of October 2025 says visitors are to be steered to two central garages, Geerts Willigen and the still-to-be-built Burgemeester Kuperusplein garage, by making street parking dearer than the garages, with no net loss of capacity [13].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The Burgemeester Kuperusplein garage is the main project. A proposal of November 2022 asked for an investment credit of 14.7 million euros for an underground garage of about 350 spaces, and a later proposal, probably from 2024, asked for 9.4 million euros more, raising the total to 24.1 million, and reported a delay of almost a year [11][10]. We found no final decision, and the October 2025 programme still calls the garage still to be built [13]. Since September 2025 the market has moved to the northern part of the plein while the Sieversstraat and Gemeenteplein area is redeveloped, and the traffic decision says there is ample room in the Geerts Willigen garage and at Veldschans on the busiest moments [7]. The Veldschans lot was to be made permanent with about 150 spaces, with works from February 2025 [17]. Around the stadium, the Gebiedsvisie A32 of May 2025 states intentions to extend the paid-parking regime up to the A32 and improve more than 2,000 spaces, which is not yet in force [12]. The municipality had about 80 public charging locations with 200 charge points in 2025 [14].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The municipality sets the tariffs of its Geerts Willigenplein garage: 1.90 euros an hour with a daily maximum of 7.00 euros, and subscriptions of 40 euros a month on weekdays or 60 euros for all days [3]. The national register lists the P+R Stationsplein as a 144-space park-and-ride operated by Nederlandse Spoorwegen, with 1.14 euros an hour and 9.02 euros a day, entered in June 2021, and we cannot tell whether it is the area covered by the municipal station-west rates [8]. A survey of March 2022 for the eastern centre found Saturday afternoon the busiest, with 407 of 560 spaces occupied (73 percent), a single count for one area [9]. On match days the club tells supporters to use its lots, which need a card, or the free carpool site Plein Noord, and the municipality and police will check strictly for wrongly parked cars [16].

Our data cover the P+R Stationsplein, with 144 spaces, for about 61 days since 22 August 2026. Occupancy averaged about 20% on weekdays and 9% at weekends, with a peak of 73% around midday on a Thursday. The garages and street parking are not in our data.
